[1, 2] This followed the U.S. Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) actions; on September 11, 2023, the FDA approved the updated Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccines and authorized them for emergency use in younger age groups. [1] <3> On October 3, 2023, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) amended the emergency use authorization (EUA) for the updated Novavax COVID-19 vaccine for individuals aged 12 and older. [1, 3] The full approval applies to individuals 12 years of age and older, while emergency use authorization (EUA) was granted for its use in individuals from 6 months through 11 years of age. Researchers were notified of the decision on Friday, May 30, 2025.
